3 Lesson Hook: Real-World Story
Context
In 1929, the stock market had been rising for years, and most people thought it would keep going up forever. Prices fell very quickly. Most traders panicked and tried to get out of the market.

But there was a very unusual person — Jesse Livermore. Can you guess what he did?
Quiz
What did Jesse Livermore do?
AHe closed all his trades and left the market
BHe bought more stocks because he thought prices would rise
CHe added more money to his bet that the market would fall
DHe stopped trading completely and waited
The Answer
✓ CORRECTOption C
Livermore did something very bold — instead of closing his trade, he added more money to his bet that the market would keep falling. In the end, this trade reportedly made him around $100 million (in 1929 dollars), which would be worth many billions today.
Good trading is not about guessing correctly.
It's about staying calm and following your plan when everyone else is emotional.
💡 A short lesson hook will immediately spark attention, land the theory in the real world and motivate the user to become a customer
